title: Is listening to a book better than reading it
paragraphs: Picture yourself sitting at home in a quiet reading nook, ignoring the world around you, engrossed in a tale. You read the blurb, instantly became intrigued and now you’re in the middle of an absolute page-turner. But, there’s a hot debate – physical books vs. e-books vs. audiobooks. Does the device you’re using to read affect your reaction to the book?

Generally, reading uses several areas of the brain. There’s attention span, reasoning, reading fluency, memory and language comprehension. Reading is known to strengthen communicative ability, vocabulary and increase emotional intelligence and social perception. So, whichever way you’re reading, there are definitely benefits.

But, let’s look at the pros to reading with your eyes – that’s physical books and e-books. They can help to retain information better. This is because when you can actually see the words, your attention is held more closely. Add to this the fact that with physical books you can go back and find any part you missed, especially if your mind wanders, which it likely will at some point or other.

On the other hand, there’s the audiobook. Headphones in, you’re switched off from life and the story really comes alive, almost like watching a film – in your head. From a scientific perspective, listening to an audiobook is likely to help you develop a greater sense of empathy as you hear the emotion of the narrator. We can more easily understand inflection and intonation. Hearing the story engages different parts of the brain, heightening the intensity and imagery, making you enjoy it more. Yet, going back to attention span, with an audiobook it’s true that it’s much harder to go back and listen again.

All in all, it seems that there are advantages to both physical books and audiobooks. Perhaps, next time you find yourself browsing bookshop shelves, also consider the format. It may just change your whole literary experience.

vocabulary.entry: reading nook /ˈriːdɪŋ nʊk/ 阅读角
vocabulary.example: She created a cozy reading nook by the window with a soft chair and a lamp.
vocabulary.translation: 她在窗边布置了一个温馨的阅读角，摆了一把软椅和一盏灯。

vocabulary.entry: engrossed in /ɪnˈɡrəʊst ɪn/ 全神贯注于
vocabulary.example: He was so engrossed in the game that he didn't hear the doorbell.
vocabulary.translation: 他全神贯注地玩游戏，连门铃响了都没听见。

vocabulary.entry: blurb /blɜːb/ n. 书籍简介；内容提要
vocabulary.example: The blurb on the back of the book made me want to read it immediately.
vocabulary.translation: 书背面的简介让我立刻就想读这本书。

vocabulary.entry: intrigued /ɪnˈtriːɡd/ adj. 感兴趣的；被吸引的
vocabulary.example: I was intrigued by the idea of living in a different country for a year.
vocabulary.translation: 在异国生活一年的想法让我很感兴趣。

vocabulary.entry: page-turner /ˈpeɪdʒ tɜːnə(r)/ n. 引人入胜的书；扣人心弦的读物
vocabulary.example: The mystery novel is a real page-turner that you won't want to put down.
vocabulary.translation: 这本悬疑小说非常引人入胜，让人爱不释手。

vocabulary.entry: attention span /əˈtenʃn spæn/ 注意力持续时间
vocabulary.example: Young children have a short attention span and get bored easily.
vocabulary.translation: 幼儿的注意力持续时间很短，很容易感到无聊。

vocabulary.entry: reasoning /ˈriːzənɪŋ/ n. 推理；理性思考
vocabulary.example: The test is designed to assess students' logical reasoning skills.
vocabulary.translation: 这项测试旨在评估学生的逻辑推理能力。

vocabulary.entry: reading fluency /ˈriːdɪŋ ˈfluːənsi/ 阅读流畅度
vocabulary.example: Regular reading practice can greatly improve a child's reading fluency.
vocabulary.translation: 规律的阅读练习能大幅提升孩子的阅读流畅度。

vocabulary.entry: language comprehension /ˈlæŋɡwɪdʒ ˌkɒmprɪˈhenʃn/ 语言理解能力
vocabulary.example: This course is designed to develop students' language comprehension and expression.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程旨在培养学生的语言理解和表达能力。

vocabulary.entry: communicative ability /kəˈmjuːnɪkətɪv əˈbɪləti/ 交际能力
vocabulary.example: Playing team sports is a good way to improve children's communicative ability.
vocabulary.translation: 参加团队运动是提升孩子交际能力的好方法。

vocabulary.entry: emotional intelligence /ɪˈməʊʃənl ɪnˈtelɪdʒəns/ 情商
vocabulary.example: Emotional intelligence is just as important as academic ability in the workplace.
vocabulary.translation: 在职场上，情商和学业能力同等重要。

vocabulary.entry: social perception /ˈsəʊʃl pəˈsepʃn/ 社交洞察力；社会感知能力
vocabulary.example: Good social perception helps you understand other people's feelings and intentions.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的社交洞察力能帮你理解他人的感受和意图。

vocabulary.entry: retain information /rɪˈteɪn ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃn/ 记住信息；保留信息
vocabulary.example: Taking notes while studying is an effective way to retain information.
vocabulary.translation: 学习时做笔记是记住信息的有效方法。

vocabulary.entry: mind wanders /maɪnd ˈwɒndəz/ 走神；思绪飘走
vocabulary.example: My mind often wanders during long and boring meetings.
vocabulary.translation: 开冗长无聊的会议时，我经常走神。

vocabulary.entry: at some point or other /æt səm pɔɪnt ɔː(r) ˈʌðə(r)/ 迟早；在某个时候
vocabulary.example: We all make mistakes at some point or other in our lives.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在人生中迟早都会犯错。

vocabulary.entry: comes alive /kʌmz əˈlaɪv/ 变得生动有趣；活灵活现
vocabulary.example: The story really comes alive when she reads it aloud with different voices.
vocabulary.translation: 她用不同的声音大声朗读时，这个故事变得格外生动。

vocabulary.entry: sense of empathy /sens əv ˈempəθi/ 共情能力；同理心
vocabulary.example: Teaching children to care for animals can develop their sense of empathy.
vocabulary.translation: 教孩子爱护动物能培养他们的共情能力。

vocabulary.entry: narrator /nəˈreɪtə(r)/ n. 叙述者；朗读者
vocabulary.example: The narrator's deep voice made the audiobook even more enjoyable.
vocabulary.translation: 朗读者低沉的嗓音让这本有声书更具听感。

vocabulary.entry: inflection /ɪnˈflekʃn/ n. 语调变化；声调起伏
vocabulary.example: Her voice had a slight inflection when she said she was happy for him.
vocabulary.translation: 她说为他高兴时，嗓音里有一丝微妙的语调变化。

vocabulary.entry: intonation /ˌɪntəˈneɪʃn/ n. 语调；声调
vocabulary.example: Good intonation is important for clear communication in a foreign language.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的语调对外语的清晰交流至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: heighten /ˈhaɪtn/ v. 增强；加深；提高
vocabulary.example: The soft music heightened the romantic atmosphere of the evening.
vocabulary.translation: 轻柔的音乐加深了夜晚的浪漫氛围。

vocabulary.entry: intensity /ɪnˈtensəti/ n. 强烈程度；紧张感
vocabulary.example: The intensity of the storm meant we had to stay indoors all day.
vocabulary.translation: 这场暴风雨的猛烈程度让我们不得不一整天待在室内。

vocabulary.entry: imagery /ˈɪmɪdʒəri/ n. 意象；形象描述
vocabulary.example: The poet uses vivid imagery of the sea to express his feelings of freedom.
vocabulary.translation: 这位诗人用生动的海洋意象来表达他对自由的感受。

vocabulary.entry: browse /braʊz/ v. 浏览；翻阅（书籍、商品等）
vocabulary.example: I like to browse in bookshops on weekends, even if I don't buy anything.
vocabulary.translation: 我喜欢周末去书店逛逛，即便什么都不买。

vocabulary.entry: literary experience /ˈlɪtərəri ɪkˈspɪəriəns/ 阅读体验；文学体验
vocabulary.example: Reading a physical book offers a very different literary experience from an audiobook.
vocabulary.translation: 读纸质书带来的阅读体验和听有声书截然不同。

sentences.chinese: 想象一下，你坐在家里一个安静的阅读角，对周遭的一切都视而不见，沉浸在一个故事里。

sentences.english: You read the blurb, instantly became intrigued and now you’re in the middle of an absolute page-turner.
sentences.chinese: 你读了书籍简介，瞬间被勾起了兴趣，此刻正在读一本让人欲罢不能的好书。

sentences.english: But, there’s a hot debate – physical books vs. e-books vs. audiobooks.
sentences.chinese: 但一直以来都有一个激烈的争论——纸质书、电子书和有声书，哪种更好？

sentences.english: Does the device you’re using to read affect your reaction to the book?
sentences.chinese: 你用来阅读的载体，是否会影响你对这本书的感受？

sentences.english: Generally, reading uses several areas of the brain. There’s attention span, reasoning, reading fluency, memory and language comprehension.
sentences.chinese: 通常来说，阅读会调动大脑的多个区域，包括注意力持续时间、逻辑推理、阅读流畅度、记忆力以及语言理解力。

sentences.english: Reading is known to strengthen communicative ability, vocabulary and increase emotional intelligence and social perception.
sentences.chinese: 众所周知，阅读能提升沟通能力、扩充词汇量，还能增强情商和社会洞察力。

sentences.english: So, whichever way you’re reading, there are definitely benefits.
sentences.chinese: 因此，无论你选择哪种阅读方式，都必然能从中获益。

sentences.english: But, let’s look at the pros to reading with your eyes – that’s physical books and e-books.
sentences.chinese: 不过，我们来看看用眼阅读的好处——这里指的是纸质书和电子书。

sentences.english: They can help to retain information better. This is because when you can actually see the words, your attention is held more closely.
sentences.chinese: 这种阅读方式能帮助人们更好地记住信息，因为当你能直观看到文字时，注意力会更加集中。

sentences.english: Add to this the fact that with physical books you can go back and find any part you missed, especially if your mind wanders, which it likely will at some point or other.
sentences.chinese: 此外，读纸质书的时候，你可以随时翻回去查看错过的内容，尤其是在你走神的时候——这种情况或多或少总会发生。

sentences.english: On the other hand, there’s the audiobook.
sentences.chinese: 另一方面，有声书也有其独特之处。

sentences.english: Headphones in, you’re switched off from life and the story really comes alive, almost like watching a film – in your head.
sentences.chinese: 戴上耳机，你便与现实生活隔绝开来，故事仿佛在脑海中活了起来，就像在脑袋里面看一场电影。

sentences.english: From a scientific perspective, listening to an audiobook is likely to help you develop a greater sense of empathy as you hear the emotion of the narrator.
sentences.chinese: 从科学角度来看，听有声书时，你能听到朗读者的情绪起伏，这有助于培养更强的共情能力。

sentences.english: We can more easily understand inflection and intonation.
sentences.chinese: 我们也能更轻松地捕捉到语气的抑扬顿挫。

sentences.english: Hearing the story engages different parts of the brain, heightening the intensity and imagery, making you enjoy it more.
sentences.chinese: 听故事调动的是大脑的不同区域，能增强故事的感染力和画面感，让你更投入地享受阅读。

sentences.english: Yet, going back to attention span, with an audiobook it’s true that it’s much harder to go back and listen again.
sentences.chinese: 但回到注意力的问题上，有声书确实存在一个弊端——想要倒回去重听某部分内容，操作起来会麻烦得多。

sentences.english: All in all, it seems that there are advantages to both physical books and audiobooks.
sentences.chinese: 总而言之，纸质书和有声书各有千秋。

sentences.english: Perhaps, next time you find yourself browsing bookshop shelves, also consider the format. It may just change your whole literary experience.
sentences.chinese: 或许下次你在书店书架前流连时，可以多留意一下书籍的载体形式，它说不定会彻底改变你的阅读体验。
